greek: Καὶ ποιήσεις θυσιαστήριον ἐκ ξύλων ἀσήπτων, πέντε πήχεων τὸ μῆκος καὶ πέντε πήχεων τὸ εὖρος — τετράγωνον ἔσται τὸ θυσιαστήριον — καὶ τριῶν πήχεων τὸ ὕψος αὐτοῦ.
hint: The altar is to be square, five cubits each way and three high, of wood that does not rot.

notes.text: θυσιαστήριον, an altar, one translation, plain text: from θυσιάζω, to sacrifice, the place of sacrifice.

notes.lemma: τὸ μῆκος … τὸ εὖρος … τὸ ὕψος
notes.text: Accusatives of respect after ποιήσεις, as at 25:10 and 25:23: five cubits in its length.
A clause set into the measurements, the altar square, the Hebrew's rābûaʿ yihyeh.

reading: And [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will make / produce / create, you will compose / write, you will make / represent in poetry, you will describe in verse, you will put into verse, you will bring to pass / bring about / cause, you will hold, you will act, you will work / operate|ποιέω]] altar [[out of|out of, out of / forth from, from, outside of / beyond, on, upon, for, after, in or by, by the hand of, of, in consequence, by means of, according to|ἐκ]] [[of woods|of woods, of firewood / timbers, of pieces of wood / posts, of perches, of sticks / cudgels / clubs, of collars of wood, of stocks, of planks / beam, of Crosses, of money-changer's tables, of trees|ξύλον]] [[of not liable to decay|of not liable to decay / corruption, of undigested|ἄσηπτος]], of five [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces / which joined the two horns of the bow, of horns / sides of the lyre, of distances from the point of the elbow to the end of the little finger, of cubits / ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[the length|the length, the distances, the height / tallness / stature|μῆκος]] and of five [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces / which joined the two horns of the bow, of horns / sides of the lyre, of distances from the point of the elbow to the end of the little finger, of cubits / ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[the breadth|the breadth / width, the in breadth|εὖρος]] — [[with four equal angles|with four equal angles / rectangular / square, squared, a body of men drawn up in square, multiplied into itself, perfect|τετράγωνος]] will be the altar — and of three [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces / which joined the two horns of the bow, of horns / sides of the lyre, of distances from the point of the elbow to the end of the little finger, of cubits / ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[the height|the height, the top / summit / crown|ὕψος]] of it.

greek: καὶ ποιήσεις τὰ κέρατα ἐπὶ τῶν τεσσάρων γωνιῶν· ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔσται τὰ κέρατα· καὶ καλύψεις αὐτὰ χαλκῷ.
hint: Horns rise from the altar's four corners, of one piece with it, all covered in bronze.

notes.text: κέρας, the horn of an animal, and anything that projects; the chain takes up any projection, which earlier units of the word had dropped.
You will cover them, the horns: the Hebrew has wĕṣippîtā ʾōtô, you shall overlay it, the altar.
χαλκός, copper, then metal in general, then bronze; Middle Liddell says expressly that the word is not brass, and the chain leaves brass out, as earlier units of it had not.

reading: and [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will make / produce / create, you will compose / write, you will make / represent in poetry, you will describe in verse, you will put into verse, you will bring to pass / bring about / cause, you will hold, you will act, you will work / operate|ποιέω]] [[the horns of an animal|the horns of an animal, the horn, the things made of horn, the bows, the horns for blowing, the flutes, the drinking-horns, the horn guards / pipes, the horn points, the arms / branches of a river, the wings of an army / fleet, the any projections, the mountain-peaks|κέρας]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] of the four [[of corners|of corners / angles, of joiner's squares|γωνία]]; [[out of|out of, out of / forth from, from, outside of / beyond, on, upon, for, after, in or by, by the hand of, of, in consequence, by means of, according to|ἐκ]] of it will be [[the horns of an animal|the horns of an animal, the horn, the things made of horn, the bows, the horns for blowing, the flutes, the drinking-horns, the horn guards / pipes, the horn points, the arms / branches of a river, the wings of an army / fleet, the any projections, the mountain-peaks|κέρας]]; and [[you will cover with|you will cover with, you will cover, you will cover / grasp, you will bury, you will cover / conceal, you will cover with dishonour / throw a cloud over, you will put over as a covering|καλύπτω]] them [[to copper|to copper, to metal, to bronze, to anything made of brass / metal, to a copper / caldron / urn, to a brasen mirror, to a copper coin|χαλκός]].

greek: καὶ ποιήσεις στεφάνην τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ καὶ τὸν καλυπτῆρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰς φιάλας αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰς κρεάγρας αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ πυρεῖον αὐτοῦ· καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ποιήσεις χαλκᾶ.
hint: The altar's tools follow: a rim, a cover, bowls, flesh-hooks, a fire-pan, every vessel bronze.

notes.text: στεφάνη, anything that encircles, a rim: the Hebrew has sîrōtāyw lĕdaššĕnô, its pots for removing the ashes.
καλυπτήρ, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's covering, sheath, cover, lid, and in the plural tiles, left to the plural.
φιάλη, a broad, flat vessel or bowl, the commas of the entry's adjectives joined with and.
κρεάγρα, a flesh-hook, one translation, plain text.
πυρεῖον, mostly plural in Middle Liddell, pieces of wood rubbed together for fire; one sense, plain text, in the singular. The Hebrew has maḥtōtāyw, its fire-pans.

reading: and [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will make / produce / create, you will compose / write, you will make / represent in poetry, you will describe in verse, you will put into verse, you will bring to pass / bring about / cause, you will hold, you will act, you will work / operate|ποιέω]] [[anything that encircles|anything that encircles, brim, a diadem / coronal, the brim / edge, brow of a hill / edge of a cliff|στεφάνη]] to the altar and [[the covering|the covering / sheath, the cover, the lid|καλυπτήρ]] of it and [[the broad flat vessels|the broad flat vessels / bowls, the cinerary urns, the broad flat bowls|φιάλη]] of it and the flesh-hooks of it and the piece of wood of it; and [[all|all / the whole, all, nothing but, every, everyone, every single, the whole, quite, full, of all kinds, all things, everything|πᾶς]] [[the vessels|the vessels / implements of any kind, the furniture / house-gear / utensils / chattels, the accoutrements / equipment, the baggage / luggage, the tackling / gear, the inanimate objects / things, the bodies|σκεῦος]] of it [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will make / produce / create, you will compose / write, you will make / represent in poetry, you will describe in verse, you will put into verse, you will bring to pass / bring about / cause, you will hold, you will act, you will work / operate|ποιέω]] [[of copper|of copper / bronze / brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]].

greek: καὶ ποιήσεις αὐτῷ ἐσχάραν ἔργῳ δικτυωτῷ χαλκῆν· καὶ ποιήσεις τῇ ἐσχάρᾳ τέσσαρας δακτυλίους χαλκοῦς ἐπὶ τὰ τέσσαρα κλίτη.
hint: A bronze network grate is made for it, with a bronze ring at each of its four sides.

notes.text: ἐσχάρα, the hearth, a pan of coals, an altar for burnt-offerings; the watch-fires, πυρὸς ἐσχάραι, are a phrase's, set aside.
δικτυωτός, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's made in net-fashion, latticed, trellised, and lattice.
κλίτος, which Middle Liddell gives as κλίμα II, a clime, one translation, plain text, as at 26:18.

greek: καὶ ὑποθήσεις αὐτοὺς ὑπὸ τὴν ἐσχάραν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου κάτωθεν· ἔσται δὲ ἡ ἐσχάρα ἕως τοῦ ἡμίσους τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου.
hint: The rings go beneath the grate, which reaches halfway up the altar.

notes.text: Under the grate: the Hebrew has taḥat karkōb, under the ledge, a word the Greek does not render.
ἥμισυς, the neuter genitive, of the half, after ἕως.

greek: καὶ ποιήσεις τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ φορεῖς ἐκ ξύλων ἀσήπτων καὶ περιχαλκώσεις αὐτοὺς χαλκῷ.
hint: Carrying poles of the same wood are made for the altar and sheathed in bronze.

notes.text: φορεύς, a bearer, carrier, the poles; the Hebrew has baddîm, poles. Middle Liddell's pack-, of a pack-horse, is a piece of an example, set aside.
περιχαλκόω, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's cover with brass or copper, citing this verse, one translation, plain text.

greek: καὶ εἰσάξεις τοὺς φορεῖς εἰς τοὺς δακτυλίους, καὶ ἔστωσαν οἱ φορεῖς κατὰ τὰ πλευρὰ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἐν τῷ αἴρειν αὐτό.
hint: The poles run through the rings along the altar's sides, for lifting it.

notes.text: You will lead in, active, with Moses the subject: the Hebrew has wĕhûbāʾ, shall be brought, passive.
πλευρόν, a rib, the ribs, the side, the neuter, as Middle Liddell files it beside πλευρά.
ἐν with the articular infinitive, in the taking up.

greek: κοῖλον σανιδωτὸν ποιήσεις αὐτό· κατὰ τὸ παραδειχθέν σοι ἐν τῷ ὄρει, οὕτως ποιήσεις αὐτό.
hint: The altar is hollow, of planks, made as it was shown on the mountain.

notes.text: κοῖλος, hollow, an adjective here: the chain takes its senses as an adjective, and leaves to the noun the hold, the vale, the valley, a hollow, cavity, ravine, the cavities.
σανιδωτός, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's planked, boarded over, citing this verse.
παραδείκνυμι, the aorist passive participle, the thing exhibited; the middle's to exhibit, bring forward is left out.

greek: Καὶ ποιήσεις αὐλὴν τῇ σκηνῇ· εἰς τὸ κλίτος τὸ πρὸς λίβα ἱστία τῆς αὐλῆς ἐκ βύσσου κεκλωσμένης, μῆκος ἑκατὸν πηχῶν τῷ ἑνὶ κλίτει·
hint: The court begins: on the south-west side, hangings of twisted linen a hundred cubits long.

notes.text: αὐλή, the court-yard, the court or quadrangle, any court or hall.
The article τό, neuter with κλίτος, over the phrase, the thing; λίψ, the SW. wind, one sense, plain text. The Hebrew has negbâ têmānâ, the south side.
ἱστίον, any web, a sail, one translation; Middle Liddell's sail and the sails, from its examples, are repeats, set aside.

greek: καὶ οἱ στῦλοι αὐτῶν εἴκοσι, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν εἴκοσι χαλκαῖ, καὶ οἱ κρίκοι αὐτῶν καὶ αἱ ψαλίδες αὐτῶν ἀργυραῖ.
hint: Twenty pillars stand on twenty bronze bases, with silver rings and bands.

notes.text: Of them, the neuter, the hangings.
ψαλίς, a pair of scissors, a vaulted building: the Hebrew has ḥăšuqêhem, their bands.
κρίκος, a ring, for the Hebrew wāwê, hooks.

reading: and [[the pillars|the pillars, the supports / bearings|στῦλος]] of them twenty, and [[the steppings|the steppings / steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps / feet, the those whereon one stands / bases|βάσις]] of them twenty [[of copper|of copper / bronze / brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]], and [[the rings|the rings, the eyelet-holes|κρίκος]] of them and [[the pairs of scissors|the pairs of scissors, the buildings with a pointed stone roof / vaults|ψαλίς]] of them [[silver|silver / of silver|ἀργυροῦς]].

greek: οὕτως τῷ κλίτει τῷ πρὸς ἀπηλιώτην ἱστία, ἑκατὸν πηχῶν μῆκος· καὶ οἱ στῦλοι αὐτῶν εἴκοσι, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν εἴκοσι χαλκαῖ, καὶ οἱ κρίκοι καὶ αἱ ψαλίδες τῶν στύλων καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν περιηργυρωμέναι ἀργύρῳ.
hint: The east side matches it: a hundred cubits, twenty pillars, silver-cased fittings.

notes.text: Toward the east wind: the Hebrew has ṣāpôn, north. ἀπηλιώτης, the wind that comes from the rising sun, the east wind.
περιαργυρόω, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's case, plate with silver, its passive citing this verse; the perfect participle.
ἄργυρος, white metal, silver; Middle Liddell's white is the gloss of ἀργός, from which it derives, set aside.

greek: τὸ δὲ εὖρος τῆς αὐλῆς τὸ κατὰ θάλασσαν ἱστία πεντήκοντα πηχῶν· στῦλοι αὐτῶν δέκα, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν δέκα.
hint: On the seaward side the court is fifty cubits across, on ten pillars.

notes.text: The article τό, neuter with εὖρος, over the phrase, the thing; toward the sea, the west, as the Hebrew yām.

greek: καὶ εὖρος τῆς αὐλῆς τὸ πρὸς νότον ἱστία πεντήκοντα πήχεων· στῦλοι αὐτῶν δέκα, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν δέκα.
hint: The south side is fifty cubits as well, on ten pillars.

notes.text: Toward the south: the Hebrew has qēdmâ mizrāḥâ, eastward, toward the sunrise.

greek: καὶ πεντεκαίδεκα πήχεων τὸ ὕψος τῶν ἱστίων τῷ κλίτει τῷ ἑνί· στῦλοι αὐτῶν τρεῖς, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν τρεῖς.
hint: One side of the entrance has hangings fifteen cubits high on three pillars.

notes.text: The height: the Hebrew gives fifteen cubits of hangings lakkātēp, for the side, with no height.
πεντεκαίδεκα, fifteen, one word.

reading: and of fifteen [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces / which joined the two horns of the bow, of horns / sides of the lyre, of distances from the point of the elbow to the end of the little finger, of cubits / ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[the height|the height, the top / summit / crown|ὕψος]] [[of the any webs|of the any webs / sails|ἱστίον]] to the clime [[to the one|to the one, to a single one / one alone, to the same|εἷς]]; [[pillars|pillars, supports / bearings|στῦλος]] of them three, and [[the steppings|the steppings / steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps / feet, the those whereon one stands / bases|βάσις]] of them three.

greek: καὶ τὸ κλίτος τὸ δεύτερον, δέκα πέντε πηχῶν τῶν ἱστίων τὸ ὕψος· στῦλοι αὐτῶν τρεῖς, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν τρεῖς.
hint: The other side of the entrance is the same, written 'ten five' cubits, on three pillars.

notes.text: Ten five, two words, where 27:14 has πεντεκαίδεκα, one.
δεύτερος, the neuter with κλίτος; where the chain gives the adjective with the article a noun of its own, the thing.

reading: and the clime [[the second|the second, the thing coming in second, the next best, the next, the thing after, the secondly / next / afterwards / a second time, the second time, the secondary, the second of two|δεύτερος]], of ten of five [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces / which joined the two horns of the bow, of horns / sides of the lyre, of distances from the point of the elbow to the end of the little finger, of cubits / ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[of the any webs|of the any webs / sails|ἱστίον]] [[the height|the height, the top / summit / crown|ὕψος]]; [[pillars|pillars, supports / bearings|στῦλος]] of them three, and [[the steppings|the steppings / steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps / feet, the those whereon one stands / bases|βάσις]] of them three.

greek: καὶ τῇ πύλῃ τῆς αὐλῆς κάλυμμα, εἴκοσι πηχῶν τὸ ὕψος, ἐξ ὑακίνθου καὶ πορφύρας καὶ κοκκίνου κεκλωσμένου καὶ βύσσου κεκλωσμένης τῇ ποικιλίᾳ τοῦ ῥαφιδευτοῦ· στῦλοι αὐτῶν τέσσαρες, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν τέσσαρες.
hint: The gate of the court has an embroidered covering twenty cubits high, on four pillars.

notes.text: κάλυμμα, a head-covering, hood, veil, covering, for the Hebrew māsāk, screen.
The height again, where the Hebrew gives twenty cubits and no dimension.
ποικιλία, a marking with various colours, embroidery; the plural's pieces of broidery left to the plural.
ῥαφιδευτής, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's stitcher, embroiderer, citing this verse.

reading: and [[to the one wing of a pair of double gates|to the one wing of a pair of double gates, to the gates of a town, to the nether world / hell, to the entrance, to the orifice, to the entrance into a country through mountains / the mountain-pass, to the narrow straits|πύλη]] [[of the court-yard|of the court-yard, of the wall of the court-yard, of the court / quadrangle, of the any court / hall|αὐλή]] [[a head-covering|a head-covering, a hood / veil, a covering, a grave|κάλυμμα]], of twenty [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces / which joined the two horns of the bow, of horns / sides of the lyre, of distances from the point of the elbow to the end of the little finger, of cubits / ells, of cubit-rules|πῆχυς]] [[the height|the height, the top / summit / crown|ὕψος]], [[out of|out of, out of / forth from, from, outside of / beyond, on, upon, for, after, in or by, by the hand of, of, in consequence, by means of, according to|ἐκ]] [[of hyacinth|of hyacinth, of sapphire|ὑάκινθος]] and [[of purple-fish|of purple-fish, of purple dye / purple, of purple raiment|πορφύρα]] and of scarlet [[of having been twisted by spinning|of having been twisted by spinning / spun and standing so|κλώθω]] and [[of a fine flax|of a fine flax, of linen made from it|βύσσος]] [[of having been twisted by spinning|of having been twisted by spinning / spun and standing so|κλώθω]] [[to the marking with various colours|to the marking with various colours / embroidering / embroidery, to the varied aspect / diversity, to the versatility / subtlety / craft|ποικιλία]] [[of the stitcher|of the stitcher / embroiderer|ῥαφιδευτής]]; [[pillars|pillars, supports / bearings|στῦλος]] of them four, and [[the steppings|the steppings / steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps / feet, the those whereon one stands / bases|βάσις]] of them four.

greek: πάντες οἱ στῦλοι τῆς αὐλῆς κύκλῳ κατηργυρωμένοι ἀργυρίῳ, καὶ αἱ κεφαλίδες αὐτῶν ἀργυραῖ, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν χαλκαῖ.
hint: Every pillar round the court is silvered, with silver capitals and bronze bases.

notes.text: καταργυρόω, the perfect passive participle: covered with silver, and the passive's own silvered, and bought or bribed with silver.
κεφαλίς, for the Hebrew wāwêhem, their hooks.

reading: [[all|all / the whole, all, nothing but, every, everyone, every single, the whole, quite, full, of all kinds|πᾶς]] [[the pillars|the pillars, the supports / bearings|στῦλος]] [[of the court-yard|of the court-yard, of the wall of the court-yard, of the court / quadrangle, of the any court / hall|αὐλή]] [[in a circle|in a circle / ring / round about|κύκλῳ]] [[having been covered with silver|having been covered with silver and standing so, having been silvered and standing so, having been bought / bribed with silver and standing so|καταργυρόω]] [[to a piece of silver|to a piece of silver / silver coin, to money / a sum of money / cash, to silver|ἀργύριον]], and [[the parts of a shoe|the parts of a shoe, the heads / chapters|κεφαλίς]] of them [[silver|silver / of silver|ἀργυροῦς]], and [[the steppings|the steppings / steps, the steps, the powers to step, the rollings, the those with which one steps / feet, the those whereon one stands / bases|βάσις]] of them [[of copper|of copper / bronze / brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]].

greek: τὸ δὲ μῆκος τῆς αὐλῆς ἑκατὸν ἐφʼ ἑκατόν, καὶ εὖρος πεντήκοντα ἐπὶ πεντήκοντα, καὶ ὕψος πέντε πηχῶν, ἐκ βύσσου κεκλωσμένης, καὶ αἱ βάσεις αὐτῶν χαλκαῖ.
hint: The whole court: a hundred by a hundred, fifty by fifty, five cubits high.

notes.text: A hundred upon a hundred: the Hebrew has mēʾâ bāʾammâ, a hundred by the cubit; its fifty by fifty the Greek keeps.

greek: καὶ πᾶσα ἡ κατασκευὴ καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐργαλεῖα καὶ οἱ πάσσαλοι τῆς αὐλῆς χαλκοῖ.
hint: All the court's fittings, tools and pegs are bronze.

notes.text: κατασκευή, preparation, equipment, fixed furniture; ἐν κατασκευῇ, in preparing for, is a phrase's, set aside.
ἐργαλεῖον, a tool, instrument, one translation run.
πάσσαλος, a peg, a gag.

reading: and [[all|all / the whole, all, nothing but, every, everyone, every single, the whole, quite, full, of all kinds|πᾶς]] [[the preparation|the preparation, the equipment, the any kind of furniture that is fixed, the building / fixture, the any furniture, the state / condition / constitution, the device / trick|κατασκευή]] and [[all|all / the whole, all, nothing but, every, everyone, every single, the whole, quite, full, of all kinds, all things, everything|πᾶς]] [[the tools|the tools / instruments|ἐργαλεῖον]] and [[the pegs|the pegs, the gags|πάσσαλος]] [[of the court-yard|of the court-yard, of the wall of the court-yard, of the court / quadrangle, of the any court / hall|αὐλή]] [[of copper|of copper / bronze / brasen, brasen|χαλκοῦς]].

greek: Καὶ σὺ σύνταξον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ισραηλ καὶ λαβέτωσάν σοι ἔλαιον ἐξ ἐλαίων ἄτρυγον καθαρὸν κεκομμένον εἰς φῶς καῦσαι, ἵνα κάηται λύχνος διὰ παντός.
hint: Israel is to bring pure beaten olive oil, so that a lamp burns continually.

notes.text: ἔλαιον, olive-oil, its genitive plural by the accent: ἐλαία's, the olive, would be ἐλαιῶν. Oil out of oils.
ἄτρυγος, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's without lees, clarified, pure, citing this verse.
καθαρός, clear of dirt, clean; the chain takes up clear of guilt, purified, without blemish and clear, exact, which earlier units of the word had dropped.

κόπτω, the perfect passive participle, struck, beaten; the middle's senses, to beat one's breast, to mourn for, are left out. Where the active's English has its object inside a phrase, κ. τὴν χώραν to cut down the trees in it, to lay it waste, the passive is said in English's own way, the land the subject: having had the trees in it cut down, having been laid waste.
Through all, παντός neuter, continually, as at 25:30.

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of Genesis 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")

greek: ἐν τῇ σκηνῇ τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἔξωθεν τοῦ καταπετάσματος τοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς διαθήκης καύσει αὐτὸ Ααρων καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ ἀφʼ ἑσπέρας ἕως πρωὶ ἐναντίον κυρίου· νόμιμον αἰώνιον εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ.
hint: Aaron and his sons tend the lamp from evening to morning, a statute for all generations.

notes.text: Will light: the Hebrew has yaʿărōk, shall set in order.
Of the covenant, διαθήκη, where the Hebrew has hāʿēdut, the testimony.
The article τοῦ, neuter with καταπέτασμα, over the phrase, of the thing.
Of you: the Hebrew has lĕdōrōtām, their generations.
